tools.name: mcp__netagent__get_config_section
tools.description: Return one section of the running config as raw text (e.g. section='router ospf', 'vlan', 'interface ethernet2', 'access-list'). Full config is never available.

device.description: Device name from the topology, e.g. leaf1

tools.name: mcp__netagent__get_interfaces
tools.description: Interface status summary for a device (link state, vlan, speed, duplex). Pass 'interface' (e.g. ethernet2) for full detail on one interface.

device.description: Device name from the topology, e.g. leaf1

tools.name: mcp__netagent__get_ip_interfaces
tools.description: L3 interfaces with IP/mask. On switches: SVIs and routed ports. On Linux hosts: addresses AND the routing table incl. default gateway.

device.description: Device name from the topology, e.g. leaf1

tools.name: mcp__netagent__get_ospf_neighbors
tools.description: OSPF neighbor table of a device: neighbor id, state (FULL/EXSTART/...), interface.

device.description: Device name from the topology, e.g. leaf1

tools.name: mcp__netagent__get_routes
tools.description: IP routing table of a device. Optionally filter by destination prefix or address.

device.description: Device name from the topology, e.g. leaf1

tools.name: mcp__netagent__get_topology
tools.description: Discovered LLDP neighbor map of the whole network — which port connects to which device. Good first call.

tools.name: mcp__netagent__get_vlans
tools.description: VLAN database and trunk status (allowed/native VLANs per trunk) of a switch.

device.description: Device name from the topology, e.g. leaf1

tools.name: mcp__netagent__ping_from_device
tools.description: Ping an IPv4 address FROM the given device (switch or host). Returns raw ping output. count is capped at 5.

device.description: Device name from the topology, e.g. leaf1

source.description: Optional source interface (switches only), e.g. vlan10

tools.name: mcp__netagent__submit_diagnosis
tools.description: Submit your FINAL diagnosis and end the session. Call exactly once, only when confident. fix_commands are proposed to a human — they are never executed automatically.

device.description: Device where the root cause lives

fault_class.description: One of the known fault class names

root_cause.description: One-sentence root cause, specific (interface, VLAN id, IP...)

fix_commands.description: Commands a human would apply to fix it
